label: Tab Item
title: Tab Item
summary: Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.
corePrinciple: One view, one short label, and always inside Tabs.

anatomy.title: A label and an underline
anatomy.description: A Tab Item is a pressable label with 8 px above and below. When selected, its label turns black and a 2 px gold underline spans the tab’s full width.
blocks: Its view is on screen now.
Shown only while the tab is selected.
Names the view in a word or two.

anatomy.note: Its view is on screen now.

configuration.title: A label, and a spoken name when needed
configuration.description: A Tab Item has no size, icon, or style options: you set its label and, when a view needs a count, the counter badge from Figma.
blocks: The label is also what screen readers say.
Short labels such as AY24 get a full spoken name: “Assessment year 2024”.

states.title: Idle and active
states.description: The screen marks the tab whose view is showing as active; a Tab Item never selects itself. Pressing dims it to 70% until release. There is no disabled state.
blocks: Black label and a gold underline across the tab.

examples.title: Active
examples.description: Black label and a gold underline across the tab.

sizing.title: 33 px tall; Tabs sets the width
sizing.description: A Tab Item is 33 px tall: a 17 px label with 8 px above and below. It is as wide as its label; Tabs places the tabs 16 px apart.

content.title: One or two words that name the view
content.description: Write a noun in sentence case, such as “Statements”. Don’t write actions like “Download” or long phrases; when a label must be abbreviated, give the tab a spoken name.

inContext.title: Tax years over one panel
inContext.description: Each Tab Item belongs to a Tabs row. The screen marks one active and swaps the panel when another is pressed; the abbreviated labels each have a spoken name.

doDont.title: Keep each tab in its row
doDont.description: Each pair shows a Tab Item used as intended versus one that confuses people.
blocks: The row places the tabs 16 px apart.
A lone Tab Item stretches across its container with no row around it.
One underline shows the current view.
Only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

sources.title: Use Tab Item through Tabs
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma subcomponent with the installed package and the Tabs stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Tab Item is a subcomponent: in Figma it lives in Coin Subcomponents and reaches designs through the Tabs slot. Figma’s variants are State Idle and Active, each with a counter badge; the package shows the badge when a count is set. The published Storybook has no Tab Item stories yet, so the story links show Tabs. On the web a tab is announced by its label or spoken name and whether it is selected. Only the selected tab is in the Tab order; Enter and Space select a tab, and the arrow keys move between tabs.
